analysis.title: US Market Intelligence Morning Briefing (October 21, 2026)
key_insights: Yesterday's rally in stocks and breadth, with RTY outperforming, followed US-Iran deal headlines. JPM sees little real progress and reads the move as short covering rather than growing confidence. Desk flow supports this: volumes ran about 32% lower and clients hesitated to re-gross.

Overnight AI sentiment got a lift from SPCX's earnings beat and SMCI's upside preannouncement. JPM says these two alone do not resolve investor concerns about AI financing risk and the scale of AI capex. Attention now turns to META earnings.

Pre-market SPCX is +9.4% after Q3 sales rose 161% to $14.6B (vs $12.8B expected), with the Super Intelligence segment profitable for the first time. SMCI is +12.3% after raising FQ1 sales guidance to $18.5-19.5B (vs $14.9B expected). NFLX is -6.2% pre-market on a soft Q4 guide and weaker ads.

French 10Y yields rose another 5-6bp and touched 5% for the first time since 2002. The OAT-Bund spread is near 150bp on fiscal and political worries. UK September CPI rose to 3.5% YoY (vs 3.4% survey, 3.1% prior), and OIS still prices a 25bp BoE hike on Nov 5.

JPM's tactical stance is bullish. Last week's selloff was driven by the Momentum/Tech Unwind and AI Credit Fears risks the desk had flagged, while earnings (ASML, TSMC) and consumer data stayed healthy. JPM expects the rotation out of Tech to continue at a slower pace.

JPM prefers cyclical exposure outside Tech, selective buying of Tech weakness in Semis and Memory (possibly via defined-risk options), and large-cap Banks (XLF) on the recent pullback. The Monetization Menu also keeps Financials and Retailers, Brazil and Japan, and Reopening names to watch if energy prices fall.

The key catalysts JPM names are the inflation component of this week's PMIs, the Oct 28 Fed meeting (a hold would remove residual hike risk, with focus on the FY27 path), rates stabilization, and META and NVDA GTC Berlin as tests of AI monetization.

META buyside bar: the stock is up nearly 40% from ~$550 lows two months ago and sentiment is very strong. Focus is on the 2027 Opex and Capex guide, Muse KPIs, and a possible equity raise if the stock is above $800.
META Q3 expectations: revenue bogey ~$64B (+26% Y/Y FXN), Street ~$63.25B, guide range $61-64B. Q4 revenue Street ~$73.5B, with investors expecting a guide of $72-75B.

META 2027 expectations: Street Opex ~$203B is seen as too low, with buyside expecting a guide of roughly $210/215B to $220/225B. Street Capex ~$200B is seen as too low versus buyside $225-250B. Buyside Opex plus Capex is $435-475B (midpoint $455B). Street 2027 EPS is $34, which could fall to ~$32 on a heavy Opex guide, and Street 2028 EPS is ~$39.

Earnings macro read-through from COF, SYF, ALLY, MMM, UAL and GE points to resilient consumer spending and credit. COF's domestic card charge-off rate fell to 3.98% (down 65bp Y/Y) and SYF's net charge-off rate was 4.79% (down 37bp from 5.16%).

Companies are passing through higher energy and tariff costs. MMM raised its oil cost estimate to $185M from $150-175M, on top of about $280M of tariffs. UAL recaptured 50% of higher fuel expense in Q2 and expects 80-90% in Q3 and full recovery by Q4. JPM says this could keep inflation pressure sticky.

SPCX first take from JPM's Stuart Humphrey: Q3 revenue $14.6B vs $12.7B Street, Adj. EBITDA $8.8B vs ~$6.6B Street, Super Intelligence revenue $7.6B vs $6.5B, and nameplate compute rose to 1.7GW. The pushbacks are capital intensity, earnings quality after the Cursor close, and upside already priced in. 1.3bn shares become eligible for sale off lockup on Thursday Oct 22.

NFLX first take from Mark Schilsky: Q3 operating margin was much better than feared, but the Q4 revenue guide was 1 point shy of expectations, internal ad revenue estimates fell 10% for the year, Q4 margin was a touch weak, and there was little on 2027. The stock was trading -3%.

JPM TMT desk: high-touch volumes remain anemic ahead of a heavy catalyst calendar (SPCX and NFLX tonight, META, TXN and LRCX tomorrow). Sentiment in semis is precarious with no real signs of risk adding. The desk expects hyperscaler prints to reinforce 2027 capex plans.

earnings_insights: SPCX Q3 2026 (reported 10/20 after close): revenue $14.6B reported vs $12.7B Street estimate (another section cites $12.8B expected). Adj. EBITDA $8.8B vs ~$6.6B Street estimate. Super Intelligence revenue $7.6B vs $6.5B Street estimate, Connectivity $5.25B vs $4.84B, Space $1.77B vs $1.41B.
SMCI preannounced after the 10/20 close: FQ1 sales guidance raised to $18.5-19.5B vs $14.9B expected (consensus estimate).

NFLX Q3 (reported 10/20): Q4 revenue guide about 1 point below investor expectations, internal ad revenue estimates down 10% for the year, Q3 operating margin better than feared, Q4 operating margin a touch weak, little said on 2027.

META Q3 2026 preview (reports 10/21 after close): revenue guide $61-64B, Street estimate ~$63.25B, buyside bogey ~$64B (+26% Y/Y FXN). Q4 revenue Street estimate ~$73.5B (+24% Y/Y FXN), with buyside expecting a guide of $72-75B.

META 2027 estimates (preview, not reported): Street Opex ~$203B vs buyside $210-230B, Street Capex ~$200B vs buyside $225-250B, Street EPS $34 (could fall to ~$32), 2028 Street EPS ~$39. 2026 Opex guide $165-169B and Capex guide $130-145B.
COF reported: domestic card charge-off rate 3.98%, down 65bp Y/Y. SYF reported: net charge-off rate 4.79% vs 5.16% a year earlier, with delinquency rates in line with the prior year.

MMM reported: raised oil cost estimate to $185M from $150-175M, plus about $280M of tariffs, and said pricing fully offsets the pressure. UAL reported: recaptured 50% of higher fuel expense in Q2, expects 80-90% in Q3 and full recovery by Q4.
Earnings due Oct 21: ABT, CCI, CME, CSX, DHR, ELV, IBM, KMI, LRCX, LUV, LVS, META, NEE, PM, T, TMO, TSLA, TXN, URI and others.

tension_points.bull_case: SPCX and SMCI results lifted AI sentiment, and JPM expects hyperscaler prints to reinforce 2027 capex plans and the return-on-investment case for datacenter builds.
tension_points.bear_case: Two positive catalysts alone would not resolve concerns about financing risk and the scale of AI capex, and sentiment in semis is precarious with no real signs of risk adding.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A tech earnings miss, or META and NVDA failing to show revenue delivery, spending plans and demand visibility.

tension_points.bear_case: JPM reads the move as short covering with little evidence of real progress, lower volumes and clients hesitant to re-gross.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US-Iran deal would squeeze EU and RTY higher, per JPM's older menu.

tension_points.bull_case: Muse success and a stock up nearly 40% off lows could push it toward $800+ if management delivers surprises.
tension_points.bear_case: A 2027 Opex guide above the Street's ~$203B could cut 2027 EPS estimates from $34 toward ~$32, and a post-Q3 equity raise is considered likely.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Opex guided toward the low end of $210-225B and a stock below roughly $800 would weaken the equity raise and further upside case.
